claim: Phuket Elephant Sanctuary is observation-only, refuses bathing interactions to avoid stressing elephants, and is phasing out even feeding interactions from 1 April 2026.
quote: if people crowd around or interact with them during this bathing ritual, it becomes stressful for the elephants, preventing them from displaying their natural behavior... discontinue all feeding interactions

claim: Phuket Elephant Sanctuary charges roughly ฿3,000 adult / ฿1,500 child for a half-day and operates a no-touch policy, while Green Elephant still allows mud-spa contact and Elephant Jungle Sanctuary actively breaks the no-touch standard.
quote: Half-day ฿3,000 adults/฿1,500 kids; no touching policy (unless the elephant engages first) ... Green Elephant Sanctuary Park ... they still allow a mud spa with elephants ... Elephant Jungle Sanctuary ... promote feeding and playing with the elephants, which is against the 'no touch policy'

claim: Riding causes long-term spinal damage to elephants and prevents them from feeding adequately, so there is no ethical version of an elephant-riding camp.
quote: Riding can cause long-term damage to an elephant's spine and lead to painful conditions, such as osteoarthritis. Additionally, consuming as much as 10% of their body weight in food every day simply isn't possible if elephants are forced to carry tourists around all day.

claim: Tiger temple-style attractions involve hand-rearing, caging and trafficking; the Kanchanaburi Tiger Temple raid found 147 live tigers and dozens of dead cubs in freezers.
quote: 147 tigers were removed from the 'temple,' while the bodies of more than three dozen deceased tiger cubs were found in freezers

claim: Phuket Elephant Sanctuary is a joint project between former camp owner Montri Todtane and Lek Chailert of the Save Elephant Foundation, anchoring its conservation credibility.
quote: joint partnership between Mr. Montri Todtane, a previous Phuket elephant camp owner and world-renowned elephant rescuer and conservationist Lek Chailert, founder of Save Elephant Foundation

claim: The Gibbon Rehabilitation Project sits inside Khao Phra Thaeo, Phuket's last evergreen rainforest, and rescues gibbons taken from the wild for the photo-prop tourism trade.
quote: Baby gibbons are deliberately taken from the wild to be used for tourism...In order to obtain a baby gibbon, its whole family is killed.

claim: Khao Phra Thaeo Wildlife Sanctuary spans 22 km² and hosts the rare Langkow Palm (Kerriodoxa elegans) along with gibbons, langurs, slow loris and mouse deer.
quote: The sanctuary spans 22 square kilometers and is a haven for gibbons, boars, mouse deer, langurs, slow loris ... Langkow Palm (Kerriodoxa elegans), one of the world's rarest palms

claim: John Gray's Sea Canoe is the original Phang Nga Bay operator — Gray discovered the hidden hong lagoons by kayak in 1989 and runs a strict no-touch / no-loud-talk eco-policy.
quote: caves and hidden lagoons John Gray found in 1989 ... visitors are asked to respect nature by not touching, no loud talking and no smoking

claim: Phang Nga day-trip operators are differentiated by time on water: better outfits spend hours at each hong / cave while budget tours give 30–60 minutes per stop.
quote: the company spending the majority of the day exploring multiple cave sites and lagoons (compared to other companies offering only 30-60 minutes)

claim: Phuket's surf season runs May–October during the southwest monsoon, with Kata producing 2–5 ft beginner-friendly waves, Kalim a 3–6 ft reef break for experienced surfers, and Nai Harn offering occasional clean peaks for beginner-to-intermediate riders.
quote: From May to October, waves here usually reach about 2–5 feet – just right for learning ... Kalim Beach is known for its reef break ... 3–6 feet during peak times ... Nai Harn ... beginner to intermediate surfers

claim: Kalim is a shallow coral right-hand reef break with 50–100 m rides and waves up to 3 m; Surin offers barrel waves and strong currents for skilled surfers only.
quote: a shallow coral right-hand reef break offers long rides of 50 to 100 metres ... Surin Beach ... barrel waves ... heavier wave action and strong currents

claim: Hanuman World runs 16 ziplines and 30+ platforms with a 400 m longest line, plus a skywalk and a new dual-track Hanuman Luge (650 m and 1.2 km), with packages from ฿1,990 to ฿3,490.
quote: 16 world-class ziplines over 400 metres long ... 30+ platforms ... Hanuman Luge ... 2 tracks ... 650M and 1.2KM ... World A+: ฿3,490

claim: Hanuman World and Flying Hanuman are sister companies; Hanuman World is the larger, more feature-rich park (luge, skywalk, restaurant) while Flying Hanuman is zipline-only.
quote: Flying Hanuman has only ziplines, while Hanuman World has ziplines and a zipline roller coaster, and is much bigger with a very nice restaurant

claim: Tiger Muay Thai in Chalong has run since 2003 and is Thailand's best-known Muay Thai / MMA camp, training everyone from first-day beginners to UFC fighters with daily drop-in classes.
quote: Tiger Muay Thai in Phuket is Thailand's #1 Training Camp, with daily classes of Muay Thai, Fitness, MMA, BJJ, Yoga & much more

claim: Most Phuket camps accept walk-in students with single classes at ฿500–800 and day passes at ฿700–1,000, making a one-off training session viable on a weekend trip.
quote: Single classes cost 500 to 800 Baht. Day passes run 700 to 1,000 Baht ... most camps welcome drop-ins without booking

claim: Sinbi Muay Thai in Rawai, founded by champion Khun Sing, runs three full-size rings and is the camp travelers pick when they want serious sparring rather than fitness Muay Thai.
quote: Founded by champion Muay Thai boxer Khun Sing, Sinbi Muay Thai has a large open-air training centre with three full-size rings
